summary:
"Exam Arena.apk" (7.1 MB, file dated 2026-09-02, at /Users/harshahirrao/Speed gym/apk/Exam Arena.apk) is a Capacitor-wrapped Next.js (App Router, static export) hybrid Android app — package com.examarena.app, versionCode 1, versionName 1.0, minSdk 24, targetSdk/compileSdk 36, built with Android Gradle Plugin 8.13.0, and it is a DEBUG build (android:debuggable=true) with only the INTERNET permission, no native libraries, a single Capacitor MainActivity, and 4 Capacitor plugins (@capacitor/app, device, preferences, share). The web payload in assets/public is a full PWA (Serwist service worker, Tailwind, GSAP, React Query, Zustand, Dexie, zod) branded "Exam Arena — Competitive Learning Platform" ("Not a coaching platform. A competitive battlefield where India's sharpest minds fight, rank, and rise"), domain examarena.com, lime-on-black theme (#C8FF5A on #050505).

The app is unambiguously the same product as Speed Gym / VMSG, rebranded: its exam domains are vedic-math, gmat, cat, gre, banking (SSC/UPSC appear on the landing page), and its 15 static technique pages are Vedic-math speed techniques (nikhilam-base-100, nikhilam-base-1000, vert-cross-2digit, direct-division, digital-root, lcm-gcd, prime-factorization, number-system-factors, percentage-tricks, speed-distance, work-rate) plus exam-technique pages (data-sufficiency, quant-comparison, sentence-correction-parallelism). Dashboard routes cover sprint (+ configure-sprint, results, results/analysis), duel, practice, play, mastery, learn, flashcards, planner, explorer, feed, clubs, friends, leaderboard, achievements, analytics, history, questions, reports, notifications, settings, profile, onboarding.

A major bonus: two chunks (app/layout.js and app/dashboard/learn/page.js) were accidentally shipped as webpack dev builds with eval-source-map, leaking the original TypeScript sources (built on Windows at D:\Exam-Arena-Frontend\). I recovered 70 source files into the scratchpad. They reveal: the app currently runs entirely on MOCK data (IS_MOCK = NEXT_PUBLIC_API_MOCK !== "false", i.e. mock by default, and NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL is empty in this build); the intended backend API contract at /api/v1 (auth/login, auth/google, auth/phone with Firebase idToken exchange, auth/refresh with refresh-token retry-on-401; dashboard/topics|radar|metrics|stats|streak|events|leaderboard|recent-activity; POST sync/{key} with known key "content/feedback"); an offline-first layer (Dexie DB "ExamArenaDB" v2 with dashboardCache keyed by trustStatus — "trusted" content cached 24h, "sandbox" content cached 1h — and a feedbackQueue); and the content schema SolveAlongTemplate (zod-validated) with concept{technique_name, category, sub_category}, difficulty 1–5, expected_time, visual_scaffold (11 scaffold types incl. arrow_matrix, place_value_chart, equation_chain, venn_diagram), worked examples with step-by-step solutions, key_reminders, common_mistakes, sourceDocumentId, and generationMethod "template" | "llm" | "converted" — a direct consumption contract for the Speed Gym RAG content factory. Render modes are quick / solve_along / guided. No websocket/matchmaking/game-server code exists (duel is mock UI); no Supabase/Firebase SDK config is baked in. Verdict: Exam Arena is the productized frontend of Speed Gym (predecessor or current branding), an early frontend-only debug APK running on hardcoded mock data, with the backend and content-factory integration designed but not yet wired in.

decisions_and_status: Exam Arena is the same product as Speed Gym under a consumer brand: Vedic-math speed training (Nikhilam, vertically-and-crosswise, direct division, digital root) fused with Indian competitive-exam prep (CAT/GMAT/GRE/Banking) — treat it as the productized frontend / predecessor build of the restarted project
This APK is an early frontend-only DEBUG build (versionCode 1, debuggable=true) running 100% on mock data — backend not wired (NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL empty, IS_MOCK default true); not shippable as-is

Frontend already fixes the backend API contract (/api/v1 auth+refresh, dashboard/*, sync/*) and the content schema (SolveAlongTemplate with sourceDocumentId + generationMethod llm/converted) — the restarted backend and content factory should conform to or consciously revise these
Trusted vs sandbox content tiers are already implemented client-side (24h vs 1h cache TTL), matching the content-factory promotion pipeline concept
Duel/multiplayer, BKT mastery engine, and realtime game server exist only as UI mock in this build — no client code for them yet
Two chunks shipped as dev builds with eval-source-map (a build misconfiguration to fix in any future release build); recovered sources are in scratchpad src_extract/ for reference
APK was inspected statically only (unzip + strings + AXML parsing); not installed or executed
open_questions: Where is the Exam-Arena-Frontend repo (it was built on a Windows D: drive — is it on this Mac at all)?
Is examarena.com live / registered, and is there a deployed backend that this APK was meant to point at via NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL?
Is 'Exam Arena' the go-forward brand for the restarted Speed Gym, or an abandoned direction?
What backend was implemented for /api/v1/sync/content/feedback and the dashboard endpoints (the described FastAPI backend), and does it match this contract?
Are the SolveAlongTemplate generationMethod values ('converted' presumably = book-extracted via OCR/RAG) already produced by the content factory, and what fills sourceDocumentId?

workstream_notes.backend: The APK freezes the expected backend contract: base {NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL}/api/v1; auth = POST /auth/login {email,password}, POST /auth/google and /auth/phone {idToken} (Firebase idToken exchange) returning {user{id,name,email,role}, token, refreshToken}, POST /auth/refresh {refreshToken} -> {token} with client auto-retry on 401; dashboard reads = GET /dashboard/topics|stats|events|recent-activity (all take ?domain=vedic-math|gmat|cat|gre|banking) plus /dashboard/radar|metrics|streak|leaderboard; offline mutation replay = POST /api/v1/sync/{key} (JSON payload, fire-and-forget batch; known key content/feedback). Client toggles real mode via NEXT_PUBLIC_API_MOCK=false. No websocket/game-server client exists yet, so the Node game server has no frontend counterpart in this build.
workstream_notes.data_extraction: The consumption schema for extracted book content is SolveAlongTemplate (zod-validated in the frontend): concept taxonomy {technique_name, category, sub_category}, difficulty 1-5, expected_time seconds, examples as ordered solution steps {step_num, operation, result, description}, key_reminders, common_mistakes, version, sourceDocumentId (corpus document linkage), generationMethod 'template'|'llm'|'converted' — 'converted' is the slot for OCR/book-extracted items (e.g. Nishit K Sinha LR/DI). Extraction output should target this shape; 11 visual_scaffold types are already enumerated client-side (arrow_matrix, place_value_chart, number_line, grid_construction, equation_chain, shape_canvas, coordinate_grid, textual_scaffold, rotation_diagram, formula_generalization, venn_diagram).
workstream_notes.rag: The client already implements the trusted/sandbox trust ladder for generated content: dashboardCache entries carry trustStatus with 24h TTL for 'trusted' and 1h for 'sandbox', implying the content factory promotes sandbox content to trusted after review/verification. User feedback on content flows through an offline-queued ContentFeedbackRequest synced to POST /api/v1/sync/content/feedback (Dexie feedbackQueue with retryCount) — this is the human-in-the-loop signal for the content factory. Render modes quick/solve_along/guided define the three consumption formats RAG-generated templates must support.
